mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS trend and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction permits (HOUST) and rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal housing demand contraction and cost-push inflation, which together depress corporate profit margins and drive negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods with HOUST decline and CPIAUCSL rise, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate output and earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during economic slowdown regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods with INDPRO < 100, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS > 100k) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods with PAYEMS growth, or the correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 238.0 in a month, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods with CPIAUCSL > 238.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in consumer credit (RSAFS) and declines in real GDP growth (GDPC1) signal excessive consumer leverage and economic slowdown, which together cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods with RSAFS rise and GDPC1 decline, or the interaction term in a regression is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.5%), a rapid payroll growth (PAYEMS > 100k) signals labor market overheating that may trigger wage inflation and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods with UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 100000, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
